subject: Action required: Region-specific outage — temporary routing & postmortem follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T07:12:00-08:00
Subject: URGENT: EU region - cloud provider routing failure impacting customer traffic

Markus / team,

Heads-up: our monitoring shows sustained loss of reachability for the eu-central-1 edge via ProviderX interconnects starting ~06:45 UTC. Latency spikes turned into 5xxs for affected tenants; BrightBank is reporting degraded inference requests (timeouts / 502).

What we know:
- ProviderX had a partial peering failure affecting a subset of POPs in eu-central-1.
- Auto-fallback to secondary POPs is working for most customers, but a small % of trafficked routes are still pinned and returning 502s.
- Impact window is ongoing; SRE is on it and opened INFRA-4892.

Immediate asks:
1) Markus — can you approve an immediate customer notification draft for BrightBank and any other impacted enterprise tenants? Keep it concise, include temporary reroute steps and whom to contact.
2) Rachel / Marissa — please prep CS + AM outreach; include the support-checklist.pdf as an attachment.
3) Monica / Karthik — collect temporary KV cache keys / routing knobs that customers can flip on their side if needed.

I started a short incident doc in Drive and attached the checklist.

Attachments: support-checklist.pdf (stub)

—Ben

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: BrightBank SRE <cloudops@brightbank.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T07:50:00-08:00
Subject: [NOTICE] Temporary reroute steps — EU region (BrightBank)

Hi Elena / BrightBank SRE team,

I’m Markus from Redwood Inference — following Ben’s alert, we wanted to confirm we’re seeing elevated error rates for BrightBank traffic that routes through ProviderX in eu-central-1. Our engineers have implemented an automated fallback, but a fraction of routes remain affected.

Actionable steps we recommend you try now (minimal risk):
- Option A (recommended): Switch endpoint DNS from api.redwood.com to api-alt-1.redwood.com for a 30–45 minute window. No key changes required.
- Option B: If you manage an explicit route prefix, set the route-priority flag to 200 (temporary) to prefer sidecar endpoints in eu-west-1.

We have attached a short checklist and a small reroute config snippet (reroute-config-snippet.json) that your SREs can paste into your router to expedite the switch. Our on-call SREs will remain on the line while you perform the change.

We will follow up with a more detailed post-incident summary and a package of logs for your audit. Please reply if you want Redwood to perform the DNS change on your behalf (we will need written confirmation).

Attachment: support-checklist.pdf, reroute-config-snippet.json

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Cloud SRE <cloudops@brightbank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightbank.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [NOTICE] Temporary reroute steps — EU region (BrightBank)

Markus,

Thanks — we can try Option A now. We’ll coordinate and report status. Two quick questions:
1) How long do you expect traffic to remain on api-alt-1.redwood.com before normal routing is safe?
2) If we switch DNS, will token/ACL validation be untouched? We cannot rotate keys during the window.

We’ll let you know when we start.

—Elena (BrightBank Cloud SRE)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: INFRA-4892 — incident notes + postmortem draft (for BrightBank)

Forwarding the initial postmortem draft and the set of logs we can share. I redacted tenant identifiers per contract prior to export.

Key findings (TL;DR):
- Root cause: ProviderX BGP flap affecting a subset of peering sessions with our eu-central-1 POPs. The flap caused asymmetric routing; our automated health checks did not detect the specific path failure pattern for ~12 minutes.
- Mitigation timeline:
  • 06:46 UTC — error surge detected (automatic paging)
  • 06:58 UTC — automated fallback executed for 88% of sessions
  • 07:10 UTC — manual route override completed for remaining sessions; BrightBank performed DNS switch at 07:05 UTC per their note and saw immediate improvement
- Customer impact: BrightBank saw a ~7 minute window of elevated 502s and up to 1.1% request loss for high-throughput endpoints.

What we are delivering to BrightBank in this package:
1) Redacted logs: eu-outage-logs-20281201.zip (attached)
2) Postmortem summary doc (Drive link)
3) Runbook changes: add path-pattern health checks + 30s BGP flap detection threshold
4) Offer: one month of unit-credit (token credit) as a gesture; pending legal approval.

Suggested external text for the postmortem (short):
"On 2028-12-01 at 06:46 UTC, a partial peering disruption from a third-party provider impacted routing to the eu-central-1 POPs used by BrightBank. Redwood’s automated fallback mitigations restored service for the majority of traffic within 12 minutes; manual intervention and a customer-initiated DNS reroute completed remediation for the remaining traffic. We are delivering redacted logs and a post-incident action plan. We apologize for the disruption and are offering a one-month usage credit while we complete root cause mitigations."

Attachments for customer: eu-outage-logs-20281201.zip, support-checklist.pdf

—Monica

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightbank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-02T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident materials + follow-up questions

Monica / Markus,

Thank you for the quick coordination and the logs. A few follow-ups from our auditors:
- Can you confirm whether KV cache entries are preserved when traffic is routed to api-alt-1.redwood.com? We observed no cache miss spike in our initial checks, but auditors want explicit confirmation.
- We will accept the token credit offer pending a short agreement addendum — please advise next steps.
- Is there an ETA for when the new path-pattern health checks will be deployed? We need that timeline for our risk register.

Also — curious: do you have an automated notification we can subscribe to that would ping our MTL team when similar peering anomalies occur?

—Elena

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightbank.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-03T15:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident materials + follow-up questions

Hi Elena — quick answers and next steps: 

1) KV cache behavior: When you route to api-alt-1.redwood.com there is an isolated prefix that preserves KV cache state for active sessions; we confirm there is no forced cache invalidation. We included a short technical note in the Drive doc.

2) Token credit: Rachel will send a one-line acceptance form and the proposed credit transaction this afternoon; legal sign-off is routine — we’ll track it under deal note DB-2028-561.

3) Health-check rollout ETA: Engineering will ship the path-pattern health checks next week (planned rollout: 2028-12-10). Karthik is the owner; he’ll send the release notes and the internal change window.

4) Notifications: We can add BrightBank to our Peering Anomaly webhook feed. That would push a short JSON payload to your URL within ~60s of an event. If you want that, reply with the endpoint and auth method and we’ll enable a trial.

Attachments: eu-outage-logs-20281201.zip (shared), link to postmortem in Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDeFgEiOuT-example

Thanks again for the prompt coordination and the clear acceptance of the temporary reroute. We’ll keep you posted on the rollout and send confirmation once the runbook changes are live.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
